newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore to expand with other regional economies.
newsitem.headline: Singapore to expand with other regional economies.

text.p: Singapore faces keen rivalry from other countries in Southeast Asia, but will continue to grow along with regional economies, the Pacific Economic Cooperation Council (PECC) said on Tuesday.

"Its reliance on exports and foreign investments to power growth will likely not diminish and it will continue to grow in tandem with the expansion of regional economies," the PECC said in its annual economic forecast.
But it said there was a need for a serious review of industrial structure.
"In particular, Singapore's heavy dependence on the electronic sector to foster growth and investment is creating a lop-sided external sector," it said.
Electronics account for nearly 60 percent of Singapore's non-oil exports, government figures show.
Despite this, the prospect for growth in the Singapore economy remains strong.
"Higher export growth, consistent inflow of foreign investments, continued regional growth...will allow the singapore economy to expand firther, PECC said.
"As a result the economy will grow by about 7.5 to 7.7 percent over the next three years," it said.
The PECC is an independent, policy oriented organistaion of business, academic and government representatives from 22 Asia-Pacific economies.
